correctness.rationale: For 0<q<1 and beta>0 the normalized Laurent basis gives a bilateral weighted shift with w_n^2=(1+beta q^{2n+2})/(1+beta q^{2n}); its difference w_n^2-w_{n-1}^2 equals the asserted positive eigenvalue. Geometric decay in both tails proves compactness and all positive Schatten powers; telescoping gives trace 1-q^2. The exact factorization (t-s)(1-q^2 ts)=0 of equal eigenvalues proves the reflection n+m=1-k at beta=q^k and rules out multiplicity above two. The rational function F(t) is strictly increasing then decreasing with unique peak t=1/q; comparison of the nearest three geometric arguments proves the global norm envelope and all equality cases. Independent exact arithmetic supplementary checker produced 67,264 comparisons; no infinite claim relies on it.

originality.rationale: The 2020 weighted Szego paper explicitly gives the same Hardy monomial norms (Katori-Shirai eq. 1.4), and Douglas-Kim explicitly recognizes multiplication as a bilateral shift; these ingredients are credited. The present result is instead the complete eigenvalue-collision parity law and sharp boundary-mass norm envelope for the positive selfcommutator. Compared primary sections treat annular reproducing kernels, Gaussian zeros, or reducing subspaces, not the derived spectral multiplicity trichotomy. Relevant annular Toeplitz spectral thesis material does not directly state the theorem. Comparisons with available mathematical-record search results show no stronger covering statement. Nonetheless an unlocated general weighted-shift result could imply this classification, so historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: The basis and weight formulas as well as the odd-power kernel-zero criterion are prior art; the new contribution is the full sharp commutator spectral and extremal classification and its comparison with the kernel zeros.
Older monographs and indexed general weighted-shift theorems could contain equivalent spectral multiplicity or norm statements even when title/abstract searches do not surface them.

value.rationale: The object is the natural coordinate multiplication operator of the two-circle weighted Hardy space. Its selfcommutator measures nonnormality; while its trace stays equal to the annular area fraction 1-q^2, its strongest spectral concentration varies sharply with boundary mass. The unique canonical unpaired top mode at odd integral logarithmic weights, complete pairings at even integral weights, and exact attained norm extrema form a natural, complete parameter classification rather than a prescribed finite slice or recomputation of the known reproducing kernel.
